title: LynxQuant - streaming & latency readiness discovery
summary: Initial discovery on p95 targets and token/sec streaming behavior. Customer leans toward hosted for time-to-value but has strong data residency and private networking concerns; exploring Dedicated or Private for predictable p95 under heavy concurrency. Agreed to run a short token-throughput benchmark and share security/compliance pack.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, and with me is Ethan, our systems SE. Can you do quick intros?
[00:08] Sara (LynxQuant): Hey, Sara here, Head of ML, been running prod models for inference, mostly batched endpoints today.
[00:13] Tomás (LQ): Tomás, platform, I own the infra side, curious about networking and VPC options.
[00:17] Priya (LQ): Priya, SRE, I'll be looking at SLOs and alerting.
[00:20] Maya: Great. Goal for today is to understand your p95 targets, concurrency profile, and whether hosted/dedicated/private fits.
[00:28] Sara: Our product is a streaming summarization feature, users get partial paragraphs as they type. We need p95 under 250ms for the first token ideally, and steady streaming under 80ms per token if possible at up to 120 concurrent streams in peak.
[00:42] Ethan (Redwood SE): Okay, that's helpful. When you say 120 concurrent streams, what's typical tokens per second per stream and average response length?
[00:50] Sara: Around 10-15 tokens/sec per stream, average completion 60 tokens, but peaks when customers paste long text — bursts to 200 tokens for some users.
[01:00] Maya: Important to capture burst behavior. Are you currently running on any cloud GPUs or a managed API?
[01:05] Tomás: We're on managed endpoints (other vendor) for prototyping, but latency has been inconsistent. We're evaluating Redwood because of the routing, fallback, and caching pitch.
[01:14] Priya: Security is a blocker. We need SOC2 type 2, SSO, KMS integration for keys, and VPC peering or private endpoint—can't send PII to shared buckets without control.
[01:24] Maya: We can do Private with a customer-controlled control plane or Dedicated with reserved capacity and VPC peering. We also have hosted but with strict egress rules and encryption at rest; for KMS you can bring your own key under Dedicated/Private.
[01:36] Sara: Okay, so tradeoff is speed to market hosted vs deterministic latency with Dedicated. How much variance do you see in p95 between hosted and dedicated in similar setups?
[01:46] Ethan: In our benchmarks for streaming on a 13B-ish model with prefix caching and optimized shards, hosted p95 for first token was ~180-300ms depending on region and load; Dedicated reduced tail by ~20-40% under high concurrency because of isolation and fixed GPU pools. But we need to run a tailored token/sec profile for your workload.
[02:06] Tomás: Can you explain prefix/KV caching impact? We saw weird cold start spikes for some users.
[02:12] Ethan: Sure. If you have repeated prefixes or short dialogues, prefix/KV cache drastically cuts compute for subsequent tokens; for streaming you get better tail behavior because KV cache avoids recompute. Cold starts occur when cache miss or new session where the runtime loads kv, which can add 60-120ms depending on model size.
[02:28] Sara: Quantization — we want to keep quality high. Is 4-bit quant common? What quality tradeoffs?
[02:34] Ethan: 4-bit and newer hybrid quant formats are common in Dedicated and Private. For some models you see negligible quality drop at 4-bit; others need 8-bit. We include model recommendations in Redwood Optimize. For strict QA you can run a shadow comparer.
[02:48] Priya: For SLOs, we need tracing and token-level latency breakdown to hook into our alerting.
[02:54] Maya: Console provides per-route token/time breakdowns and tracing hooks — you can export spans to your tracing backend.
[02:59] Sara: What's the expected cost delta between hosted and dedicated for your profile? We're cost-sensitive.
[03:05] Ethan: Very workload dependent. For steady high concurrency Dedicated is often cheaper per token due to reserved GPU pricing; hosted is better for bursty or low volume. We can model a rough estimate once we run your token/sec benchmark.
[03:18] Tomás: About the benchmark — what do you need from us to run it?
[03:21] Maya: Ideally a small representative prompt set (we can take 50-100 prompts), an expected concurrency matrix (baseline 20, peak 120), and token/sec per stream. We'll spin up a sandbox dedicated pool or hosted sim and run p95 streaming with KV caching on/off and quant profiles.
[03:36] Sara: We can provide prompts and a traffic script. How long does the benchmark take?
[03:39] Ethan: End-to-end a couple hours to run and 24-48h for full analysis including cold-start scenarios and different autoscale settings. For an initial pass we can deliver within 48 hours.
[03:49] Priya: Networking: we need private connectivity and audit logs. Does Redwood ship audit logs and integrate with our SIEM?
[03:55] Maya: Yes, audit logs and admin activity streams are available and can be forwarded to your S3 or SIEM; in Private deployments logs stay in your VPC.
[04:03] Sara: Any concerns about multi-region failover for lower latency? We have global users.
[04:07] Ethan: Smart routing allows region-based routing and automatic fallback. For strict p95 you might prefer multi-region Dedicated pools or Private instances in target regions. Cross-region fallback will add some latency but keeps availability.
[04:19] Tomás: Autoscaling — how do you handle sudden 10x bursts?
[04:22] Ethan: We support burst capacity on Dedicated and hosted; autoscale policies can pre-warm GPUs and use a small cold queue with graceful degradation to smaller models if needed. We also support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to a lower-cost model variant.
[04:35] Sara: What's the typical cold-start penalty for streaming sessions that have to load larger KV caches?
[04:40] Ethan: It varies; 120B-ish models can take seconds in worst cases, but for the 13B models you're targeting it's usually 300-800ms for cold start with disk load; with clever pre-warming and pinned KV, you can get that down to sub-200ms.
[04:54] Priya: We need to simulate worst-case: 120 concurrent first-time sessions arriving in 30s. Can Redwood handle that on Dedicated?
[05:01] Ethan: Yes, with planned reserved burst capacity and pre-warm scripts. We'll size the pool to absorb that and we have autoscaling heuristics for rapid spin-up. We'll validate in the benchmark.
[05:11] Sara: Do you support bringing our own model artifacts or only curated models?
[05:15] Maya: On Private and Dedicated you can bring your own model; on hosted we also support a curated catalog and onboarding for custom models with some security checks.
[05:23] Jared (customer): Quick ques — do you expose token-level streaming events like final vs partial tokens for our analytics?
[05:29] Ethan: Yes, the streaming protocol includes metadata for partial/final tokens and you can attach request IDs for tracing.
[05:35] Speaker 6: (inaudible)
[05:37] Priya: About compliance pack — can you share SOC2 reports and pen-test summary?
[05:41] Maya: We'll send the SOC2 and pen-test reports and a security whitepaper. For Dedicated/Private we'll detail the KMS integration and SSO flow.
[05:49] Tomás: Timeline: we want to decide in 3 weeks, pilot in 6 weeks. Is that reasonable?
[05:54] Maya: Yes, seems reasonable. We'll scope a 2-week pilot once we agree on mode (probably Dedicated sandbox) and sizing.
[06:01] Sara: Let's talk about failure modes — what happens if the Dedicated pool is saturated?
[06:06] Ethan: Policies can define overflow to a cheaper model variant or to hosted fallback, and you can set hard concurrency limits per customer to avoid noisy neighbors.
[06:14] Maya: Recap — Redwood will run a token-throughput benchmark with KV cache on/off, quantify p95 under your concurrency matrix, share security/compliance docs, and provide a cost estimate comparing hosted vs Dedicated.
[06:27] Sara: Sounds good. Can you also show us the console traces and example dashboards in the next call?
[06:32] Maya: Yes, we'll do a short demo of the console and tracing in the follow-up.
[06:36] Tomás: Thanks, we'll send prompts and traffic script by tomorrow.
[06:40] Maya: Perfect, thanks everyone.
[06:42] End of recording.
